title: NY State Assembly · District 40
area: Flushing and surrounding neighborhoods in northeastern Queens.

context.text: Incumbent Ron Kim is running unopposed. The Democratic, Republican and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were all canceled; Kim advanced from the Democratic and Working Families Party lines without appearing on the ballot, and no Republican candidate filed.

summary.text: Ron Kim is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for NY State Assembly District 40. After starting in a City Council office and working in city and state government, he was first elected in 2012 and has served since January 2013; his official biography says he is the first Korean-American elected to the New York State Legislature. He chairs the Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development Committee and sits on four other committees, and he is running unopposed in the 2026 general election.

background.text: Raised in Flushing, Queens, where his family has lived since he was 7; graduated from Riverdale Country Day School in 1997, where his official biography says he captained the football and basketball teams.

Earned a B.A. from Hamilton College and a Master's in Public Administration from Baruch College; in 2004 he was accepted into the National Urban Fellows Program, advising the Chief Education Office of the Chicago Public Schools while earning his degree.

Began his public-service career in then-City Council Member John Liu's office, later worked as an aide to then-Assemblyman Mark Weprin, and held posts at the NYC Department of Buildings and Department of Small Business Services.

Joined the staff of City Council Speaker Christine Quinn as a Policy Analyst in 2006, then served as a Regional Director for Government and Community Affairs in the administrations of Governors Eliot Spitzer and David Paterson (2007-2010).

After leaving the Governor's office he worked as a legislative advocate for children with special needs, small business and vulnerable New Yorkers; Ballotpedia names the Parkside Group as his employer.
Elected to the Assembly in 2012 to a seat vacated by Grace Meng, who was running for Congress; Ballotpedia lists his tenure as beginning January 1, 2013, and he has been re-elected through 2024.

According to his official biography, in his first term he wrote the "Community Corner Cafe Fund" legislation, in his second term he worked with Governor Cuomo on nail-salon industry reforms, and he collaborated on legislation establishing the Asian Lunar New Year as a New York City school holiday, announced by the mayor in June 2015.
Chaired the Assembly Task Force on New Americans starting in 2015 and served as Secretary of the Majority Conference starting in 2017.

Currently chairs the Committee on Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development and is a member of the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, Education, Governmental Operations, and Housing committees.
Ran in the February 26, 2019 special election for New York City Public Advocate, receiving 2.8% of the vote; Jumaane Williams won.
His official biography says he lives in Flushing with his wife and two daughters.

priorities.text: His official biography describes a career focused on quality education, funding for local schools, and support for small businesses in the Flushing community.

positions.summary: Sponsored A00970, which would require companies to pay an annual tax if the chief executive's compensation is 100 to 250 times the median pay of all their employees.
Cosponsored A1466, the New York Health Act (2025–26 session), which would create a universal single-payer health plan (New York Health) for state residents.

record.text: Chairs the Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development Committee; also serves on the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, Education, Governmental Operations, and Housing committees in the 2025-2026 session.
Sponsored A00676, imposing an additional tax on income attributable to long-term capital gain; referred to the Ways and Means Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.
Sponsored A00970, imposing a tax related to executive compensation; referred to the Ways and Means Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.
Sponsored A00651, requiring courts to advise noncitizen defendants of deportation risk before accepting a guilty plea; referred to the Codes Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.
Sponsored A10333, relating to maximum hours for home care aides; referred to the Labor Committee as of February 2026, not enacted as of September 2026.

researchNotes: Kim is running unopposed in the November 2026 general election, so this file covers only his record. His record draws on his official NY Assembly biography, committee page, sponsored-bill listing and individual bill status pages, plus the repo's assembly-ny.json roll-call snapshot.
